strategy.summary: CART-12 prices the cart at checkout with a bulk discount (10% off at 10+ items summed across lines), the SAVE5 coupon ($5 off after the bulk discount, floored at $0, other codes refused) and shipping ($4.99, free when discounted goods reach $50, nothing for an empty cart). The tests exercise the exported `cartTotal` in src/cart.js at unit level with Vitest. Reading the code, `bulkDiscount` uses `> BULK_THRESHOLD` instead of `>=`, so a cart of exactly 10 items gets no discount; TC1 will expose this and be kept as an expected failure with a recorded defect.
inScope: cartTotal pricing: bulk discount, SAVE5 coupon, unknown coupons, shipping thresholds, empty cart
Boundaries: 9/10 items, $49.99/$50 goods, coupon larger than goods
outOfScope: Any UI or checkout flow beyond the pricing module (the repo contains only src/cart.js)
assumptions: The checkout price is what `cartTotal(items, { coupon })` returns, rounded to cents; tests assert its return value.
A refused coupon is signalled by `cartTotal` throwing an Error; tests check it names the submitted code (the part the test controls).
Constants (BULK_THRESHOLD etc.) are imported from src/cart.js where the test needs them, rather than repeated.
openQuestions: Are coupon codes case-sensitive (is `save5` refused)? The code refuses it; the ticket doesn't say, so no case asserts it.

risks.description: Off-by-one at the bulk threshold: the code uses `>` 10 rather than `>=` 10, contrary to AC1 and its own doc comment.
risks.mitigation: TC1 tests exactly 10 items split over two lines; TC2 tests 9 items.

risks.description: Coupon applied before the bulk discount gives a different total.
risks.mitigation: TC4 picks amounts where the two orders give different totals.

risks.description: Shipping threshold checked against the pre-discount subtotal.
risks.mitigation: TC9 uses a cart whose subtotal is over $50 but whose discounted goods are under.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cart with 10 or more items in total (sum of line quantities) gets 10% off its subtotal; fewer than 10 gets no bulk discount.
Coupon SAVE5 takes $5 off after the bulk discount and the goods never cost less than $0; any other coupon code is refused with an error.
Shipping is free when goods after discounts cost $50 or more, otherwise $4.99; an empty cart costs $0.

defects.title: Cart of exactly 10 items gets no bulk discount
defects.description: AC1: a cart with 10 or more items in total should get 10% off its subtotal. src/cart.js bulkDiscount uses `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD` (strictly greater), so exactly 10 items gets no discount; BULK_THRESHOLD's own doc says "at least this many". Fix: `>=`.
defects.evidence: cartTotal([{price:2,quantity:6},{price:2,quantity:4}]) returns 24.99 ($20 + $4.99 shipping) instead of 22.99; the it.fails test passes, i.e. the assertion fails.

review.standard: Arrange / Act / Assert, one behaviour per test (test-unit-guidelines: one action per test)
review.summary: The empty-cart test makes two separate calls to `cartTotal` and asserts both, so it covers two behaviours: an empty cart costs nothing, and SAVE5 on an empty cart doesn't go below $0 or add shipping.
review.failureScenario: If the empty-cart shipping rule broke (for example `items.length === 0` was dropped, so `cartTotal([])` returns 4.99), the first assertion would fail and stop the test. The SAVE5 call would never run, and the failure would carry the same title whichever of the two broke. Splitting it into two `it` blocks, or an `it.each` over the two option sets, would report each one separately.
